# Makori (formerly Mako)

> Site: https://mako-lang.com
> Longer reference: https://mako-lang.com/llms-full.txt
> Repo: https://github.com/loreste/mako

Version **0.6.29** (alpha). Compiled language, `.mko` sources, native (Cranelift) + C + LLVM backends, no GC.
Ownership model actively hardened — O(1) RC array clone, position-aware
last-use move, scope-exit destructors. Safety validated under ASan, UBSan,
TSan with zero errors across 448 test files. `unsafe`, the C runtime, and
FFI are outside the safety model.

Write new code with: `fn`, `let`, `on Type {}`, `pack` / `pull` / `export`,
`hold` / `share` / `arena`, `crew` / `kick` / `join` / `fan`, `match`,
`switch` / `case`. Older dual forms (`func`, `:=`, `import`, `package`) still
parse; do not prefer them. See docs/IDENTITY.md if you care about the style bar.

> **Renamed from Mako.** The language is now called **Makori**. The `mako`
> command still works as a backward-compatible alias, and `.mko` file extension
> is unchanged.

## Key rules for generating Mako code

1. **No semicolons.** Statements are newline-terminated.
2. **No parentheses around conditions.** Write `if x > 0 {` not `if (x > 0) {`.
3. **Braces required.** Even single-line if/for bodies need `{ }`.
4. **Always qualify imports.** `pull "io"` then `io.read_file(...)`, never bare `read_file`.
5. **Structs are value types.** `let a = b` copies. `mut` params pass by pointer.
6. **Owned fields are freed at scope exit.** Strings, arrays, maps in structs are
   automatically freed. Don't manual-free.
7. **`append` returns a new header.** Always `xs = append(xs, v)`.
8. **Errors must be handled.** Unused `Result` is a compile error. Use `?` or `match`.
9. **No null.** Use `Option[T]` — `Some(v)` or `None`.
10. **Test functions:** `fn TestFoo() { assert(...) }` in `*_test.mko` files.

## Short facts

- Generics: `fn id[T](x: T) -> T`, `struct Pair[T]`, `enum Box[T]`,
  bounds `fn f[T: Iface](x: T)` — all monomorphized. Write `Pair[int] { … }`.
- `mut self` on methods: `fn push(mut self, v: int)` — mutations persist in caller
- Multi-statement lambdas: `fn(x) { let a = x + 1; return a }` — full control flow
- Stdlib in Mako: `pull "io"`, `pull "encoding/json"`, `pull "context"`,
  `pull "net/http"`, `pull "database/sql"`, `pull "collections"`,
  plus Go-equivalent packs (`strings`, `bytes`, `slices`, `os/env`,
  `net/netip`, `math/bits`, `hash/crc32`, `crypto/rand`, `crypto/hkdf`,
  `image`, `testing/quick`, …). `concat` ≡ Join; `matches` ≡ Match.
- Tuples / multi-return: `let a, b = f()` (incl. struct elements)
- Methods: `on Type { fn m(self) -> T { ... } }`
- Modules: `pack name`, `pull "path"`, always qualify: `pkg.fn`, `eng.Table`,
  `eng.Point { x: 1 }`, `eng.Red` / `eng.Color.Green(n)`
- Maps: keys `int|string|float|bool|Struct|Enum`; values same, `[]T`/`[][]T`,
  nested maps depth ≤3, bags `Option`/`Result` (incl. nests, channels),
  tuples `(T,U[,…])` (bag/chan fields), `chan[T]`; `[]Option`/`[]Result`;
  `maps_*`. Map monomorph C helpers are demand-driven (only used shapes).
- Struct/enum `==` `!=` structural (strings by content)
- Channels: `make(chan[T], n)` / `chan_open[T](n)` for int/bool/float/string/struct/enum/tuple
- `chan_len` / `chan_cap` work on any `chan[T]` (not only int rings)
- Kick Send: Copy, string, deep-POD structs, Option/Result/tuple of sendables, chan handles
  (not maps/arrays/non-POD). Prefer `chan[Struct]` for multi-field worker results.
- Loops: `for i, v in range s` / `for k, v in range m` / C-style `for`
- F-strings: `f"hello {name}, age {age}"` — stack-based builder, zero malloc for short strings
- `string_view` / `str_as_view` / `str_to_owned` — zero-copy views; owning strings free at scope exit
- Stack POD array lits `[a,b,c]` — no malloc; empty `[]` allocates nothing
- Format: `fmt_sprintf*` / `fmt_sprint*` for printf-style verbs
- Dispatch: `match` on strings/ints/enums; `switch`/`case` on values
- Parallel work: `fan(xs, fn(x) { x * x })`
- Concurrency: `crew` / `kick` / `join`, channels, `select`, `actor`
- Scheduler: `sched_set_workers(n)` opt-in pool (0 = one pthread per kick)
- Channel string take: `chan_str_send_take` / `chan_str_try_send_take` (move; no clone)
- Build: locked deps verified at compile (`mako.lock` content hashes)
- `+= -= *= /= ++ --`, `a, b = b, a`, `let x = if c { a } else { b }`
- `if init; cond { }`
- Ownership: hold, share, arena — no GC
- Errors: `Result` / `Option`, `?`, unused Result is an error
- Checked math: `checked_add` / `sub` / `mul`, `would_overflow_*`
- Const fn: `const fn f(n: int) -> int` with match/while/for/break/continue/strings
- First-class functions: `fn` values, closures capture POD + string + struct by value
- Iterator protocol: struct with `fn next(self) -> Option[T]` usable in for-range
- Release: `-O3 -flto`. WASM: `wasm32-wasip1`
- Stdlib: HTTP (incl. HTTP/2), TLS, SQL, crypto, regex, UUID/ULID, channels,
  SIP signaling, SMTP, templates, domain storage (BTree/LSM/WAL/Bloom),
  Go-equivalent application packs (see docs/STDLIB.md)
- Speed: wyhash maps, zero-copy string comparisons, compile-time constant folding,
  stack-based f-strings, condvar channel select, atomic HTTP conn tracking

HTTP/2 note: DATA frames larger than 16384 are split automatically. Empty
string `""` is a singleton — do not raw-free it.

## Debugging & tracing

- `dbg(x)` — works on any type (int, float, bool, string). Prints
  `[dbg] file.mko:42: x = value` to stderr and returns the value unchanged.
  Use inline: `let y = dbg(compute())`.
- `dbg_str(s)` — string-specific variant (still works).
- `MAKO_TRACE=1 ./binary` — prints function entry/exit with source locations.
  Zero overhead when not enabled.
- Panics print a Mako-level stack trace with function names and source locations.
- `mako debug file.mko` — interactive lldb session with Mako data formatters.
- `mako dap` — DAP adapter for VS Code. Debugger shows user variable names
  only (codegen temporaries are filtered).
- `mako check --json=v1` — structured JSON diagnostics for editor integration.
- `--sanitize address|thread` — ASan/TSan builds.
- `stack_trace()` — print current call stack at any point.
- `error_chain(err)` — print error with full source-location trace.

## Ownership model (0.6.29)

Mako uses compile-time ownership tracking with no garbage collector:

- **Owned values** (strings, arrays, maps, structs with owned fields) are freed
  at scope exit automatically.
- **`mut` params** are passed by pointer. The caller retains ownership.
- **Last-use move**: when an owned local is used for the last time, the compiler
  moves it (zero-copy) instead of cloning. This includes strings.
- **O(1) array clone**: `[]struct` clone is an RC retain, not a deep copy.
  Append COWs when the buffer is shared.
- **Scope-exit destructors** run for all owned locals, including struct fields
  and call-result temporaries.
- **No use-after-free**: the codegen tracks liveness and prevents moved values
  from being read.

Common patterns:
```mko
// Struct with owned fields — freed automatically
let db = Database { tables: make([]Table, 0, 1), name: "mydb" }

// Return transfers ownership to caller
fn make_db() -> Database {
    let db = Database { tables: make([]Table, 0, 1), name: "new" }
    return db  // moved, not copied
}

// mut param: caller keeps ownership, callee borrows via pointer
fn add_table(mut db: Database, t: Table) {
    db.tables = append(db.tables, t)
}
```

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/loreste/mako/releases/latest/download/install-release.sh | bash
```

From source: `make install` → `~/.local/bin/mako`

## Quick start

```bash
mako init hello --name hello
cd hello
mako run main.mko
mako build main.mko
```

## Hello world

```mko
fn main() {
    print("hello from makori")
    print(fib(10))
}

fn fib(n: int) -> int {
    if n <= 1 {
        return n
    }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
}
```

## Common patterns

### HTTP server
```mko
pull "net/http"

fn main() {
    let mux = http.new_mux()
    mux.handle("/", fn(w: http.ResponseWriter, r: http.Request) {
        w.write("hello world")
    })
    http.listen_and_serve(":8080", mux)
}
```

### JSON parse + serialize
```mko
pull "encoding/json"

struct User { name: string  age: int }

fn main() {
    let u = json.unmarshal[User]("{\"name\":\"alice\",\"age\":30}")
    print(u.name)
    let s = json.marshal(u)
    print(s)
}
```

### Concurrency
```mko
fn main() {
    let ch = make(chan[int], 10)
    crew t {
        let job = t.kick(fn() -> int {
            return expensive_work()
        })
        ch.send(42)
        let result = job.join()
        print(result)
    }
    let val = ch.recv()
    print(val)
}
```

### Error handling
```mko
fn parse_port(s: string) -> Result[int, string] {
    let n = str_to_int(s)?
    if n < 1 || n > 65535 {
        return Err("port out of range")
    }
    return Ok(n)
}

fn main() {
    match parse_port("8080") {
        Ok(n) => print(n)
        Err(e) => print(f"error: {e}")
    }
}
```

### Struct methods
```mko
export struct Point { x: int  y: int }

on Point {
    fn distance(self) -> float {
        return sqrt(float(self.x * self.x + self.y * self.y))
    }

    fn translate(mut self, dx: int, dy: int) {
        self.x += dx
        self.y += dy
    }
}
```

### Tests
```mko
fn TestAddition() {
    assert_eq(2 + 2, 4)
}

fn TestStringConcat() {
    let s = "hello" + " " + "world"
    assert(s == "hello world")
}
```

## Commands

```bash
mako build file.mko              # debug build
mako build --release file.mko    # optimized (-O3 -flto)
mako run file.mko                # build + run
mako test path/                  # run test functions
mako fmt file.mko -w             # format in place
mako check file.mko              # typecheck only
mako debug file.mko              # lldb session
mako dap                         # DAP adapter (editors)
mako build --target wasm32-wasip1 file.mko -o out.wasm
```

## Stdlib (rough map)

Output, strings, math, files, HTTP server/client, HTTP/2, TLS, JSON, SQLite /
Postgres / MySQL / Redis, crypto (SHA/HMAC/bcrypt/scram/SRTP), base64/hex/gzip/tar/zip,
regex, UUID/ULID, cookies/sessions/auth, channels (int/float/string/struct/ptr),
mutex/atomics/cmap/rwmutex, event loop (epoll/kqueue), game net (UDP),
SIP signaling, SMTP mail, text/html templates, domain storage (BTree/LSM/WAL/
Bloom/PageManager/SST), signals, fs watch, rate limit / circuit breaker,
checked arithmetic, overflow detection, shutdown, tracing, leak checks,
crash reporting, testing (assert/fuzz/property/snapshot/mock/fixture/coverage).
